key_insight: Biology-guided transcriptomic features captured immunotherapy response better and more consistently than data-driven gene selection in advanced urothelial carcinoma.
clinical_relevance: Transcriptomic profiling may add meaningful prediction value for atezolizumab response, but its benefit appears smaller once standard and enriched biomarkers are already included.
method: Compared knowledge-guided tumor microenvironment gene-set features vs transcriptome-wide gene selection
Evaluated incremental AUPRC gain over clinical variables and biomarker baselines in IMvigor210 (n=298)
Checked feature stability across folds and external validation performance
evidence_signal: In IMvigor210, knowledge-guided features improved AUPRC by +0.058 over clinical variables alone, but only +0.011 beyond standard biomarkers; external evaluation showed a similar pattern (+0.128 vs +0.019).
watch_item: Data-driven gene lists were unstable across folds (mean Jaccard similarity 0.227), so implementation should favor robust pathway-level representations rather than single-gene signatures.
paper_title: Incremental Predictive Value and Representation of Transcriptomic Features for Immunotherapy Response in Advanced Urothelial Carcinoma
